content.title: Antithrombotic regimens in patients with acute coronary syndrome and an indication for oral anticoagulation

key_recommendations.target_INR: Target INR of 2.0–2.5 in patients treated with VKA (except individuals with a mechanical prosthetic valve in the mitral position).
key_recommendations.anticoagulant_preference: In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) without mechanical prosthetic valves or moderate to severe mitral stenosis, use NOACs over VKAs as they reduce bleeding risk.
key_recommendations.default_strategy: Dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT) with a NOAC at the recommended dose for stroke prevention plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT), preferably clopidogrel, is recommended as the default strategy for up to 12 months after up to 1 week of triple antithrombotic therapy (TAT).
key_recommendations.TAT_definition_and_duration: TAT consists of a NOAC plus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT: aspirin + clopidogrel). The recommendation for up to 1 week of TAT is based on the median treatment duration in the investigational arm of the AUGUSTUS trial.
key_recommendations.risk_balance: Available RCTs were not designed to detect differences in ischaemic events; there is a numerically higher risk of stent thrombosis and myocardial infarction with reduced antiplatelet therapy but this is offset by lower bleeding risk, resulting in a neutral effect on total mortality.

figure_12_summary.purpose: Timeline-based antithrombotic regimens for patients with ACS and an indication for OAC.
figure_12_summary.default_strategy_timeline: 0 to up to 1 week: TAT ((N)OAC + DAPT) (Class I); up to 1 month: DAT ((N)OAC + SAPT) (Class I); 3–12 months: DAT ((N)OAC + SAPT) with step-down to (N)OAC monotherapy by 12 months (Class I). Beyond 12 months: (N)OAC monotherapy (Class I).
figure_12_summary.alternative_strategy_for_high_ischemic_r: Longer duration of combined antiplatelet + anticoagulant therapy may be considered (figure indicates strategy to reduce ischaemic risk with prolonged DAT/TAT as Class IIa/IIb options).

content.preferred_antiplatelet: Clopidogrel was used in >90% of patients in the major RCTs and is the preferred single antiplatelet therapy when combined with a NOAC.

abbreviations.ARC-HBR: Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk

evidence_and_notes.trial_basis: The recommendation for up to 1 week of TAT references the AUGUSTUS trial (median treatment duration in investigational arm).
evidence_and_notes.clinical_implication: Preference for NOACs over VKAs in non-valvular AF reflects bleeding risk reduction; however, VKAs remain indicated in patients with mechanical prosthetic valves or moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis.
evidence_and_notes.limitations: RCTs cited were not powered/designed to detect differences in ischaemic events; ischemic risk (stent thrombosis/MI) may be numerically higher with shortened antiplatelet therapy.
